findings.title: Constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: At line 73, the constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), so it validates grantType a second time and never rejects a null rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is then accepted and encodeTokenId can later produce an ID ending with the literal string "null". The argument should be rawTokenId.

findings.title: Access token ID matcher does not validate grant type shortcut
findings.body: In matchesSafely, the encoded token prefix such as "onrtac" has the grant type at indices 4-5 ("ac"), but the code calls substring(3, 5), which returns "ta". It also returns false when the substring equals the expected shortcut, which is inverted. As a result, these event assertions accept any encoded token ID regardless of its grant type and would reject a correct one if the offset were fixed. It should use substring(4, 6), guard the prefix length, and return false when the substring does not equal the expected grant shortcut.
